newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordanian soldier kills 7 Israeli schoolgirls.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian soldier kills 7 Israeli schoolgirls.

text.p: A Jordanian soldier on Thursday shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls on a field trip to a border site nicknamed "The Island of Peace."
The attack south of the Sea of Galilee put pressure on the United States to broker a swift end to the crisis in Israeli-Arab relations over plans for Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
In Washington, U.S. President Bill Clinton called the shooting "senseless" and appealed for calm in the region.
The soldier emptied the clip of his rifle into a group of girls aged 13 to 14, police and witnesses said. At least six were wounded. Soldiers overpowered the gunman, who was arrested.
Israel sent a helicopter and medical team to Jordan where some of the dead and wounded were taken.

King Hussein cut short a visit to Spain and put off a trip to Washington to return home after news of the shooting, the bloodiest attack by a Jordanian soldier on the Israel-Jordan frontier in many years.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Jordan to punish those responsible for "the murder of innocent girls".
The soldier opened fire as the seventh and eighth graders walked from three buses to look from an observation point at Syria and the Golan Heights.

"We walked around and I heard shots...It was close...I turned around and saw a soldier taking a clip from his rifle and firing and we ran to the hill...He shot me in the hand," said Ornit, one of 122 girls on an annual field trip from a school at Bet Shemesh near Jerusalem.
The girls were at a spot nicknamed "The Island of Peace", a farm area where the Jordan and Yarmuk rivers meet. Israel leases it from Jordan under their 1994 peace treaty.

"We yelled for the girls to get down and we all tried to hide," said witness Rosha Himi. "He came down and started chasing us. I saw how he inserted a new clip but with the second one he didn't manage to fire," Himi told reporters.

Apart from infiltrations by Palestinian guerrillas the heavily guarded Israeli-Jordanian frontier has been largely quiet for years. Israelis have been able to cross into Jordan since the 1994 treaty that gave Israel its warmest ties with any Arab state.

But relations with King Hussein have become icy since Netanyahu unveiled plans to build Jewish housing in East Jerusalem, which Palestinians say have plunged the whole U.S.-sponsored regional peace drive into crisis.
The king wrote to Netanyahu on Sunday accusing him of pushing Arabs and Israelis towards "an abyss of bloodshed and disaster".

"Who knows...how many of these gun-toting lunatics are waiting for the green light in the form a remark in which Israel is described the way it is being described today," Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said. Asked if he was referring to the king's letter, Levy said no.
Another Israeli cabinet minister was more explicit.
"Perhaps the conclusion is that the king must hold his tongue so that a soldier doesn't take his words to mean more than he indended," Israel's Education Minister Zevulun Hammer told army radio.

Hammer, whose pro-settlement party has threatened to quit Netanyahu's coalition government if the Jerusalem building is frozen, said: "There is a problem with the best of our neighbours. Ninety percent of the Knesset voted for this peace and look what happens just for the heck of it. No one provoked here. There was no provocation."
Only the United States has shielded Israel from international censure since Netanyahu recently gave the green light to the settlement plan.
Western officials said the shooting would temporarily take the diplomatic heat off Netanyahu, who would be able to point to Arab violence as the greatest threat to peacemaking.
Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti condemned the attack. Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat called Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh to express condolences and sorrow.
The shooting puts pressure on Washington to defuse the crisis between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat who has summoned Western and Arab envoys to a meeting in Gaza on Saturday.
Israel will not attend the meeting, which Arafat has billed as an attempt to save the peace process.
